posts.name: Hardik Azmi
posts.cooked:
Spark Program | ServiceSeal: Prepaid Utility Passes on CKB, Piloted at a Charging Kiosk in Lagos

Applicant: Hardik Azmi (GitHub: DegenerateAlchemist (Yugi) · GitHub )
Funding requested: $900 USD
Timeline: 6 weeks
Category: CKB Application / Retail Utility & State Primitives
Repository: GitHub - DegenerateAlchemist/service-seal · GitHub
Revision (v2): Following the committee’s feedback updated the Type Script and kiosk workflow so every debit requires both the attendant’s terminal signature and the customer’s pass signature (preventing attendant-only deductions when the customer is not present) and documented the limitation and drop-off mitigations for unrecorded deductions. budget unchanged

1. Summary

Where I stay in Lagos, Nigeria power is terrible so people rely on neighbourhood charging kiosks to keep their phones, lamps and power banks working. Regular customers usually pay upfront for a few charges instead of paying every single time they drop a phone off.

I own one of these charging kiosks though I don’t run it myself daily, I have someone employed there handling customers while I’m away. Right now, prepaid balances are written down in a paper notebook at the shop. When a customer insists they paid for five charges and only used two, while the notebook says four, the customer has no way to verify the record on their own. Since I’m not sitting at the shop, I only hear about the argument after.

ServiceSeal moves that notebook record into a live CKB Cell. A customer gets a prepaid pass holding a set number of units. Each time they drop off a device to charge, my attendant logs the debit, the customer approves it with their pass key and the pass Cell updates to a new Cell with the lower balance and the next sequence number. A CKB Type Script checks that both the terminal and the customer signed the receipt, the sequence goes up by one, the balance drops by the exact amount recorded and the balance never drops below zero. Since a Cell can only be spent once, two conflicting updates can’t both go through. Both the customer and I can check the full usage history directly from CKB without relying on the notebook at the shop.

2. Team Profile

Applicant: Hardik Azmi (DegenerateAlchemist on GitHub)
Role: Full-stack and smart contract developer, and owner of the Lagos charging kiosk used for the pilot
Contact: Nervos Talk
Background: I built Stellar Kit, an open-source tool for building, deploying and simulating smart contracts on Stellar that was funded by Stellar WA. I have also built different solutions across Solana, Stellar/Soroban, Sui and EVM. On CKB, I have worked on a CKB script and built the initial TypeScript core for ServiceSeal (v0.1.0). I am new to Fiber and this proposal does not use it.

3. The Problem

Around here in Lagos, people buy most daily utilities in small retail portions: phone and battery charging, cooking gas refills, water and shared equipment time. Prepaid tabs are very common because customers like locking in credit when they have cash and shop owners want steady repeat customers.

When you own the shop but have an employee running the counter, three issues come up all the time:

  • Customer and attendant arguments: The customer has no proper receipt trail showing their starting balance and every deduction made from it.
  • Owner and attendant reconciliation: When I check in at the end of the day, I cannot tell from home if numbers in the notebook were changed, scratched out or skipped.
  • No simple tool for small retail utilities: Big companies can run custom backend databases, but for a local kiosk or gas shop spinning up a standard database still leaves the exact same trust problem since the operator can edit rows whenever they want.

4. How It Works

Terms used in this proposal:

  • Pass Cell: A live CKB Cell holding one customer’s prepaid balance for a specific terminal.
  • Terminal: The signing key used by the attendant at the kiosk to log usage.
  • Customer pass key: The customer’s signing key (kept in their phone browser or derived locally from their secret pass PIN at the counter, never stored on the kiosk) used to co-sign debits.
  • Usage receipt: A message co-signed by both the terminal and the customer pass key with the session ID, terminal ID, sequence number and units used.
  • Successor Cell: The new Pass Cell created when a usage receipt is applied.

Open pass. A pass is created on CKB testnet with a starting unit balance (like 100 units) and sequence = 0, tied to the kiosk’s terminal ID, the terminal key hash and the customer’s pass key hash.

Record usage. When a customer drops off a device to charge, the attendant enters the units used and the customer approves the debit on their phone browser (or by entering their secret pass PIN on the customer screen to sign locally). Both the terminal and the customer sign the receipt for sequence = last_sequence + 1. The transaction spends the old Pass Cell, puts the co-signed receipt in the witness and creates the Successor Cell with remaining_units = old_units - usage and sequence = old_sequence + 1.

Check history. Anyone with the pass ID can open the web page or run the CLI tool to pull every debit from CKB transaction history and check the remaining balance without calling a ServiceSeal server.

What it covers and what it doesn’t:

  1. Preventing deductions when the customer is not present (enforced on-chain by the Type Script): Because the Type Script checks both device_key_hash and customer_key_hash on every usage receipt, my attendant cannot deduct units on their own while a customer is away. Any transaction signed only by the kiosk terminal fails validation in CKB-VM. Likewise, a customer cannot alter their balance without the terminal signature.
  2. What happens if the attendant fails to record a deduction (limitation and workflow mitigation): Without a hardware meter wired into the power strip, an on-chain script cannot physically know that a phone was plugged into a wall socket if no transaction is submitted. If the attendant simply forgets to log a debit for a prepaid customer, the customer’s on-chain balance stays untouched, meaning the customer is never shortchanged (the loss falls on my kiosk, not the buyer). The real risk for me as the owner is the attendant charging a device off-book. To mitigate this in our kiosk workflow:
    • Debit on drop-off: The debit is co-signed when the customer hands over the phone, before it goes on the charging board.
    • Sequence intake tags: Every device plugged into the board gets a numbered clip showing the pass’s latest on-chain sequence number from the terminal screen. When I check in or audit the shop, every device on the charging board must match a live on-chain sequence increment for that day.
    • Customer co-sign habit: Since the customer only co-signs at drop-off for the exact units they are using right then, the attendant cannot come back later in the evening and retroactively batch-deduct an “unrecorded” charge without the customer present.

5. Technical Architecture

Already built (not funded by this grant):
The repository (v0.1.0) already has the off-chain protocol logic working in TypeScript:

  • Fixed 100-byte SS01 Cell data layout (session_id, terminal_id, device_key_hash, remaining_units and last_sequence).
  • Ed25519 receipt signing and verification.
  • Sequence and balance transition checks.
  • CKB witness encoding (encodeSessionWitness) and batch transitions (applyReceiptBatch).
  • 14 rejection tests covering replay, altered usage, wrong terminal, wrong session, skipped sequence, overdraw and bad state formatting.

Funded by this grant:
ServiceSeal Type Script (CKB-VM): Enforces the SS01 transition rules on-chain (upgraded to include customer co-signing):

  • session_id, terminal_id, device_key_hash and customer_key_hash stay the same between the input and output Pass Cells.
  • output.last_sequence == input.last_sequence + 1.
  • output.remaining_units == input.remaining_units - receipt.usage and receipt.usage > 0.
  • Dual authorisation check (terminal + customer): verifies that both the kiosk terminal and the customer authorised the debit. Week 1 validates this in CKB-VM first to measure cycle cost and cell capacity (either via dual witness signatures or by pairing the Type Script with the customer’s Lock Script) before building the rest of the app around it.

Transaction Builder & Verifier CLI: TypeScript functions using CCC to open a pass, co-sign and send a debit transaction on Pudge testnet and rebuild a pass’s history straight from CKB RPC/indexer.

Kiosk Web UI (Testnet): A simple three-page web app (Open Pass, Kiosk Terminal + Customer Approval and Pass History) that my attendant and regular customers will test during a two-week pilot at the kiosk alongside our usual paper notebook.

POC Scope:

  • Testnet only (Pudge), using test units alongside normal cash/transfer payments at the kiosk.
  • Out of scope for this grant: mainnet deployment, real money custody, Fiber channels, hardware socket meters or a formal security audit.

6. Deliverables

  • ServiceSeal Type Script: CKB-VM script checking the pass rules, deployed on Pudge testnet with tests covering valid updates and invalid attempts (attendant-only debit without customer signature, replay, skipped sequence, overdraw, wrong terminal, changed identity fields and bad cell data).
  • Transaction SDK & History Verifier: Open-source TypeScript module and CLI command that builds create and co-signed debit transactions with CCC and rebuilds any pass’s history from CKB testnet RPC without a backend.
  • Kiosk Testnet Web App: Simple browser UI for opening a pass, co-signing kiosk usage and checking pass history by ID, plus a short video showing the full flow and an overdraw or attendant-only transaction getting rejected on-chain.
  • Lagos Kiosk Pilot & Report: Two-week pilot run at my charging kiosk with my employee and regular customers, written up in a final post on Nervos Talk with testnet transaction hashes, cycle and capacity numbers and honest notes on how it went.

All code will be open-source under the MIT license.

7. Roadmap

Milestone Timeline Work
1. On-chain check & script layout Week 1 Test SS01 witness and dual authorisation checks (terminal + customer) in CKB-VM, measure cycle cost and cell capacity and post the Week 1 numbers.
2. Core Type Script & rejection tests Weeks 2 to 3 Write the full Type Script and rejection test suite (attendant-only debit without customer signature, replay, overdraw, skipped sequence, wrong terminal/session and bad output size) and deploy to Pudge testnet.
3. CCC transaction builder & Web UI Week 4 Hook up CCC transaction building to the Open Pass, Kiosk Terminal + Customer Approval and Pass History pages, plus the CLI history checker.
4. Lagos kiosk pilot Week 5 Run ServiceSeal at my kiosk in Lagos alongside our paper notebook for regular customers, log real usage on Pudge testnet and note any issues my employee or customers run into.
5. Release & final report Week 6 Post the pilot transaction hashes, cycle and capacity measurements, demo video and final report on Nervos Talk.

8. Budget ($900 USD)

Area Hours / Basis Amount
CKB Type Script, rejection tests and Pudge deployment 24h × $15/hr $360
CCC transaction builder, CLI verifier and Kiosk Web UI 24h × $15/hr $360
Two-week Lagos kiosk pilot, demo video and final report 12h × $15/hr $180
Total 60 hours $900

Paid in CKB under standard Spark Program rules. I am not asking for hardware, hosting or travel costs since the pilot runs at my own kiosk during normal work hours.

9. How to Verify

Anyone reviewing the project can check the deliverables without relying on a server I control:

Deliverable How to verify
Type Script & rejection tests Clone the repo and run the test command to see valid co-signed transitions pass and invalid transitions (including attendant-only debits) fail in the script.
Deployed Pudge script Check the published script OutPoint and transaction hashes (opening a pass, valid debits and a rejected overdraw/unauthorised debit) on the Pudge testnet explorer.
History verifier CLI Run the CLI checker against any pilot pass ID using a public Pudge RPC URL with the web app turned off, and compare the balance with the explorer.
Kiosk Web UI & pilot Open the testnet web app, create and debit a test pass and check the pass transaction hashes from the Lagos kiosk pilot in the final report.

10. Ecosystem Value & Post-Spark Plans

We are building ServiceSeal as a reusable CKB primitive for prepaid, terminal-metered state transitions not a one-off app tied to my shop. The SS01 Pass Cell and Type Script give any CKB developer a ready-made primitive for services where a user locks in credit upfront and a terminal or attendant draws it down over time with co-signed receipts.

For this Spark grant, I am proving the primitive on-chain and piloting it at my own charging kiosk in Lagos where my attendant and customers already deal with notebook disputes. Once the primitive is proven in the kiosk pilot, we plan to use it as the base layer for a broader local utility pass around here because people buy most everyday essentials in retail portions such as buying cooking gas locally by the refill or prepaid water and later pair the primitive with Fiber for payment settlement.

posts.name: 行天春彦
posts.cooked:
Hi @hardik,

Thank you for continuing to follow the Spark Program and for submitting the ServiceSeal proposal.

After review by the Spark Program committee, your proposal’s status is pending. This is not a rejection, but an invitation to revise your proposal.

The committee recognizes the project’s real-world value: bringing usage tracking for prepaid services into CKB in an actual retail setting is an interesting application of state primitives.

The committee has two specific concerns about the current design:
As described in the proposal, the device that updates the Cell state is controlled by the store clerk. What happens if the clerk fails to record a deduction after a customer uses the service? Also, how can the system prevent the clerk from updating the Cell when the customer is not present—for example, by deducting service units that were never actually used? Please explain how the Type Script or the overall workflow prevents these situations, or explicitly acknowledge this limitation and propose mitigations.

Please revise the proposal in light of the feedback above. We will arrange another review as soon as possible. We believe this concept has the potential to become a real-world use case on CKB, and look forward to seeing how you further refine the design.

Best regards
xingtian
On behalf of the Spark Program Committee

posts.name: Hardik Azmi
posts.cooked: Thanks @xingtianchunyan I’ve revised the proposal- every debit now requires the customer’s pass signature alongside the kiosk terminal signature inside the Type Script (so the attendant cannot deduct units when the customer is not present) and Section 4 now covers unrecorded deductions and the drop-off workflow. The kiosk pilot and budget stay the same. Changes are in sections 1, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 9
